name: Nebuzaradan
source_summary: Nebuchadnezzar's captain of the guard, who carried out the destruction of Jerusalem's temple and walls, deported the surviving population to Babylon, executed Judah's leading officials, and personally freed Jeremiah, giving him the choice to go to Babylon or remain in the land.
family_friendly_summary: Nebuzaradan was the captain of the guard for King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon. He was sent to carry out the destruction of Jerusalem after the city finally fell, burning the temple and the king's palace and breaking down the city walls. He also led many of the remaining people of Judah away into exile in Babylon. But Nebuzaradan showed unexpected kindness to the prophet Jeremiah, who had been held as a prisoner. He personally freed Jeremiah, took off his chains, and let him choose whether to go to Babylon or stay in the land of Judah, treating him with care and respect instead of as an enemy.
adult_story: Nebuzaradan served as captain of the guard for King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and was the officer sent to carry out the final destruction of Jerusalem after its long siege (2 Kings 25:8). He burned the temple of the LORD, the king's palace, and every great house in the city, and had the Babylonian army break down Jerusalem's walls (25:9-10). He deported the remaining population, though he left some of the poorest people in the land to work as vinedressers and farmers (25:11-12). His forces also stripped the temple of its remaining bronze, silver, and gold furnishings, taking them to Babylon (25:13-17), and he executed a number of Judah's chief priests, officials, and military officers at Riblah before the king of Babylon (25:18-21). Amid this destruction, Nebuzaradan showed marked personal kindness to Jeremiah, who had been imprisoned during the siege for prophesying Jerusalem's fall. Acting on Nebuchadnezzar's specific instructions to 'look after him and do nothing harmful to him' (Jeremiah 39:11-12), Nebuzaradan had Jeremiah brought to him, released him from his chains, and offered him the choice of accompanying the exiles to Babylon under his care or remaining in the land; Jeremiah chose to stay and was placed under the protection of the newly appointed governor Gedaliah (40:1-6). Nebuzaradan's role thus combines the harsh instrument of God's judgment on Jerusalem with an unexpected moment of personal mercy toward God's prophet.
devotionals: Nebuzaradan’s story teaches us about destruction of Jerusalem; may we look to Jesus, whose grace and truth never fail.
Through Nebuzaradan’s experience of exile, God teaches us to trust His wisdom and follow Jesus faithfully.
